- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–70 range, model tends to overreact; adjust forecast toward historical mean (67–69) for next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price increases; increase forecast by 1–2% for days 25–30 if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.11, -0.28, +0.11), model misreads momentum; use weighted average of recent 3–5 sentiment values to adjust forecast direction.
